mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 2% over the prior quarter is associated with a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return due to higher discount rates eroding expected equity payoffs.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS average > 2% over the last quarter
failure_condition: In sample periods with FEDFUNDS > 2% but no inflationary pressures, 20-day forward returns are non-negative with p < 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: Rising unemployment claims (PAYEMS) coinciding with a decline in consumer payrolls (GDPC1) predict a negative 60-day S&P 500 forward return as weak labor demand suppresses corporate earnings growth.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases while GDPC1 decreases over the prior 2 months
failure_condition: In periods where PAYEMS rises but GDPC1 also rises, 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in retail sales (HOUST) above the prior quarter's trend is followed by a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return as it signals resilient consumer demand and upward earnings revisions.
candidate_trigger: HOUST exceeds prior quarter trend by > 2%
failure_condition: When HOUST spikes but corporate profit margins fall, 20-day forward returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly expansion in industrial production (INDPRO) exceeding 3% from the prior month is accompanied by a positive 5-day S&P 500 forward return as it anticipates near-term supply chain easing.
failure_condition: INDPRO shows consistent monthly declines while SPX 5-day returns remain negative in > 40% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: When the 3-month moving average of FEDFUNDS crosses above 3.5%, a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return is expected as markets anticipate a shift toward accommodative policy.
failure_condition: No significant change in 20-day forward returns during the subsequent 60 days after the trigger.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4% over three consecutive months predicts a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return as it reflects labor market tightening that can suppress wage growth.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE falls below 4% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: During periods of UNRATE < 4% but low inflation, 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent increases in both consumer confidence (not available) and retail sales (HOUST) above trend are required to generate a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return, as both signals must align for a durable demand upturn.
candidate_trigger: HOUST above trend and no contradictory supply indicators (e.g., INDPRO below trend)
failure_condition: When HOUST is above trend but industrial production is also above trend, 20-day forward returns are not positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in consumer inflation (CPIAUCSL) below 2% for two consecutive months suggests a supply-side soft landing, predicting a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL falls below 2% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: If CPIAUCSL remains below 2% but S&P 500 60-day returns are flat or negative, the hypothesis is rejected.
